item.title: Bench warrant issued for former teacher over alleged abusive video
item.description: A Bench warrant has been issued against former schoolteacher, who is accused of posting a video in which he uttered abusive words towards the Minister for Employment, Productivity and Industrial Relations, Agni Deo Singh, in 2022. Mr Kumar failed to appear before Magistrate Sufia Hamza, who subsequently issued the warrant.
item.content:encoded:
A Bench warrant has been issued against former schoolteacher, who is accused of posting a video in which he uttered abusive words towards the Minister for Employment, Productivity and Industrial Relations, Agni Deo Singh, in 2022.

Mr Kumar failed to appear before Magistrate Sufia Hamza, who subsequently issued the warrant.

It is alleged that on December 14, two years ago, Mr Kumar, while in the Suva Magistrate’s Court, secured access to a Facebook account which did not belong to him and used it to post a video on a social media platform titled ‘Power In His Voice’.

He is accused of uttering vulgarities against Mr Singh, who was the Fiji Teachers Union general secretary at the time.

The case has been adjourned to November 13.

item.title: Taxman detects fraudulent docs
item.description: FRAUDULENT tax clearance and tax compliance certificates (TCCs), including fake letters, are being circulated and falsely claiming that legitimately issued certificates have been cancelled due to a system error. The Fiji Revenue and Customs Service (FRCS) has confirmed detecting the circulation of those fraudulent and unauthorised documents saying they did not originate from the service.
item.content:encoded:
FRAUDULENT tax clearance and tax compliance certificates (TCCs), including fake letters, are being circulated and falsely claiming that legitimately issued certificates have been cancelled due to a system error.

The Fiji Revenue and Customs Service (FRCS) has confirmed detecting the circulation of those fraudulent and unauthorised documents saying they did not originate from the service.

The TCC is a certificate of compliance issued to a person as proof that the person is compliant with the filing and payment of taxes in accordance with the relevant tax laws; and it is required by law when a person applies for any registration, permit or license from any Government ministry or entity.

The FRCS has, therefore, urged businesses, government ministries and departments, statutory bodies, financial institutions, procurement entities and members of the public to exercise extreme caution and independently verify the authenticity of any certificate purportedly issued by FRCS before relying on it for any official purpose.

It has also advised relevant parties that the FRCS does not cancel, revoke, or invalidate tax clearance or tax compliance certificates through informal emails, third-party correspondence or unverified letters.

FRCS chief executive officer Udit Singh said any attempts to undermine the integrity of Fiji’s tax administration was taken very seriously.

“The circulation of fake tax certificates and fraudulent cancellation notices is a deliberate attempt to deceive businesses, government agencies, and the public and FRCS will not tolerate any activity that compromises the integrity of our systems and processes,” Mr Singh said.

He warned the creation, distribution, possession, use, or presentation of false tax documents constituted serious criminal offences and could result in investigation and prosecution under the applicable laws in the country.

“Offenders may face substantial fines, imprisonment, or both.”

Mr Singh said it was important to verify certificates through official channels before accepting them as valid.

“We strongly urge all organisations and individuals not to accept any tax certificate at face value.

“Verification should be undertaken immediately through our official certificate validation portal or directly with FRCS.”

Mr Singh further advised organisations that encounter suspicious certificates to take immediate precautionary measures.

“Where a fraudulent or suspicious certificate is identified, organisations should retain a copy of the document, suspend or pause the relevant transaction or process, and report the matter immediately to FRCS together with details of the individual or entity that submitted the document.

“Any person found to be producing, distributing, possessing, or using fraudulent tax documents will be subject to investigation and appropriate action under the law.”

item.title: Pacific telcos advised working in tandem
item.description: PACIFIC telecommunications networks must combine submarine fiber cables with complementary satellite technologies to build true resilience across island nations. Amalgamated Telecom Holdings (ATH) Group chief executive officer Ivan Fong made the comment in his address at the 2026 Pacific Fiber Conference that was held at the Sheraton Fiji Golf Resort and Spa in Nadi last week.
item.content:encoded:
PACIFIC telecommunications networks must combine submarine fiber cables with complementary satellite technologies to build true resilience across island nations.

Amalgamated Telecom Holdings (ATH) Group chief executive officer Ivan Fong made the comment in his address at the 2026 Pacific Fiber Conference that was held at the Sheraton Fiji Golf Resort and Spa in Nadi last week.

Mr Fong explained how low-earth orbit (LEO) satellite providers played a crucial role as supplemental, complementary, and emergency options for remote island markets.

He said if Starlink was not in the market today, “I’m not sure how we would have dealt with the situation in the Cook Islands”.

Mr Fong said LEO satellites, traditional microwave connections, and mobile rollout must work in tandem to deliver effective solutions to end users.

He called on Pacific governments and development agencies such as Australia’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade to work closely with private investors on marginal infrastructure projects.

Although governments frequently prioritise healthcare, water, and basic utilities above technology investments, he said digital access directly aided those essential public services.

“When we talk about connectivity and access to AI, it is in fact access to everyone,” Mr Fong said.

“Otherwise, we’re creating a new class of haves and have-nots in our own communities.”

Mr Fong urged leaders to initiate a whole-of-government dialogue with private industry to aggregate demand, mitigate investment risks, and ensure equal digital opportunities across the region.

item.title: New footpath, hall for Dreketi
item.description: Assistant iTaukei Affairs Minister Ratu Isikeli Tuiwailevu officially opened the new church hall and footpath at Dreketi in Wailevu East, Cakaudrove. The opening marked an important milestone for the church and the community.
item.content:encoded:
Assistant iTaukei Affairs Minister Ratu Isikeli Tuiwailevu officially opened the new church hall and footpath at Dreketi in Wailevu East, Cakaudrove.

The opening marked an important milestone for the church and the community.

Villagers gathered to witness the occasion and celebrate the completion of the facilities.

Traditional protocols and ceremonies were also observed as part of the program.

Villagers warmly welcomed Ratu Isikeli and other guests to the community.

The new hall is expected to provide a space for church activities and community gatherings.

The footpath will also improve access to the churchs.

Men and women of the village played an active role in the preparations and celebrations.

The occasion ended with villagers coming together to celebrate the opening of the facilities and the benefit they will bring to the Dreketi community.

item.title: Island still waiting for electricity, says Ratu Apenisa
item.description: RESIDENTS of Mali Island remain uncertain whether the long-awaited electrification project will be completed before Christmas, with no work carried out in their area over the past two weeks. Tui Mali Ratu Apenisa Bogiso said while they were informed that work was continuing, construction had yet to reach Nakawaga.
item.content:encoded:
RESIDENTS of Mali Island remain uncertain whether the long-awaited electrification project will be completed before Christmas, with no work carried out in their area over the past two weeks.

Tui Mali Ratu Apenisa Bogiso said while they were informed that work was continuing, construction had yet to reach Nakawaga.

“The electricity poles have been erected on Ligaulevu,” he said.

Ratu Apenisa said villagers were told the project would be completed before Christmas this year, but he was unsure whether that target would be achieved.

“From what we have seen, I don’t have much confidence. For the past two weeks, no workers have been here.”

Despite the ongoing project, he said Mali villagers continued to live without electricity and depended entirely on small solar systems to meet their daily energy needs.

“We have been living in the dark for quite some time.”

He said that access to reliable electricity would improve the quality of life for villagers by providing better lighting, supporting children’s education, and creating opportunities for future economic development.

In response, the acting commissioner Northern Apolosi Lewaqai said the project was expected to be completed and officially commissioned by November 2026.

Mr Lewaqai said as part of the overall electrification program, household wiring works for the three villages would commence in August 2026 under the next financial year’s budget allocation.

item.title: Migration leaves villages with empty homes
item.description: MANY homes across the three villages on Mali Island now stand empty as families relocate to Labasa in search of better education and employment opportunities. Tui Mali Ratu Apenisa Bogiso said the island’s population had steadily declined over the years as young people and their families moved to the mainland.
item.content:encoded:
MANY homes across the three villages on Mali Island now stand empty as families relocate to Labasa in search of better education and employment opportunities.

Tui Mali Ratu Apenisa Bogiso said the island’s population had steadily declined over the years as young people and their families moved to the mainland.

Ratu Apenisa said the migration was not driven by the lack of electricity or water but by the desire to access schools, jobs and improved services.

“There are not many people left. Many houses are now empty because families have moved away,” he said.

He said most families returned to the island during school holidays and special occasions to visit relatives and maintain their ties with the village.

“Despite these visits, the number of permanent residents continued to decrease, affecting daily village life and community activities.”

He said the trend showed the challenges faced by remote maritime communities where employment opportunities were limited.

“I hope that ongoing development projects and improved infrastructure would encourage more people to remain on the island or eventually return to live there.”

He said preserving the island’s communities was important to maintaining the traditions, culture and identity of the people of Mali.

item.title: 20-year wait for seawall | Villagers frustrated as Government says materials are ready for project
item.description: THE people of Nakawaga Village on Mali Island are frustrated after waiting almost two decades for a promised seawall project to become a reality. Tui Mali Ratu Apenisa Bogiso said the community had repeatedly been told the project would begin the following year, but those promises had yet to materialise.
item.content:encoded:
THE people of Nakawaga Village on Mali Island are frustrated after waiting almost two decades for a promised seawall project to become a reality.

Tui Mali Ratu Apenisa Bogiso said the community had repeatedly been told the project would begin the following year, but those promises had yet to materialise.

Ratu Apenisa said each year villagers continued to hear the same assurances, leaving many to lose confidence that the project would ever be completed.

“It has been nearly 20 years, and we are still waiting,” he said.

He said coastal erosion remained a concern for villagers, who had hoped the seawall would help protect their homes and shoreline.

“Now it is just a waiting game. Every year we hear the same promises, but nothing changes.”

He said villagers had continued to raise the issue over the years but were still waiting for tangible progress.

“The community remains hopeful that the project will eventually be delivered. The seawall is important to safeguard the village from the impact of rising seas and coastal erosion for future generations.”

In response, the acting commissioner Northern Apolosi Lewaqai said materials for the construction of the nature-based seawalls had been procured through the ministry’s internal funding allocation.

Mr Lewaqai said the project was awaiting confirmation of shipping schedules and the availability of barge transportation to facilitate the delivery of materials to the island communities.

item.title: Naivalurua seeks action over taxidriver assaults
item.description: POLICING Minister Ioane Naivalurua has referred concerns over attacks on taxidrivers in Nausori to the Eastern Division commander for closer attention. Mr Naivalurua said the issue was an operational matter that should be dealt with by the division responsible.
item.content:encoded:
POLICING Minister Ioane Naivalurua has referred concerns over attacks on taxidrivers in Nausori to the Eastern Division commander for closer attention.

Mr Naivalurua said the issue was an operational matter that should be dealt with by the division responsible.

He said the matter fell under the responsibility of the divisional commander rather than being a policy issue.

“It comes under the responsibility of the division commander.

“It’s not a policy matter. It’s an operational matter. It should be addressed and dealt with by the division commander.”

He said he had taken note of the concerns and had reminded the Eastern Division commander to look into the matter.

“I’ve noted it down. I’ve sent a reminder to the division commander to take a closer look.”

His comments come amid concerns over the safety of taxidrivers, with attacks on drivers raising questions about security while they provide public transport services.

The Fiji Times reported in June that taxi operators in the Western Division were considering refusing service to unruly passengers following a series of assaults on drivers.
